text: A. Make a fist. Rest your thumb straight up along the side of your index finger.
B. Hold four fingers straight up and together. Fold your thumb across your palm.
C. Curve your fingers and thumb into the shape of the letter C.
D. Point your index finger up. Touch your thumb to your other fingertips to make a circle.
E. Bend your fingertips down to touch your thumb, which is tucked under them.
F. Touch your index finger to your thumb to make a circle. Spread the other three fingers up.
G. Point your index finger sideways with your thumb above it, like a little beak.
H. Point your index and middle fingers sideways, held together.
I. Make a fist and raise only your pinky finger.
J. Make the letter I, then draw a J in the air with your pinky (down, then curve).
K. Point index finger up and middle finger forward. Put your thumb between them.
L. Point your index finger up and your thumb out to the side, making an L.
M. Tuck your thumb under your first three fingers.
N. Tuck your thumb under your first two fingers.
O. Curve all your fingers to touch your thumb, making an O.
P. Make a K and tip it so your fingers point down.
Q. Make a G and point it down toward the floor.
R. Cross your index finger over your middle finger.
S. Make a fist with your thumb wrapped across the front of your fingers.
T. Make a fist and poke your thumb up between your index and middle fingers.
U. Hold your index and middle fingers up together.
V. Hold your index and middle fingers up and apart, like a V.
W. Hold three fingers up and apart. Your thumb holds down your pinky.
X. Make a fist and raise your index finger in a hook.
Y. Stretch out your thumb and pinky. Fold the other fingers down.
Z. Point your index finger and draw a Z in the air.
ILY. "I love you": thumb, index finger and pinky up.

text: Sign language is a real language. People talk with their hands, face and body.
Every sign has five parts: handshape, location, movement, palm direction, and face and mouth.
Use your strong hand. Copy your teacher like a mirror, in the space in front of your body.
Fingerspelling uses one handshape for each letter. Keep your hand steady and move smoothly.
Move your lips while you sign. Shape the word with your mouth at the same time as your hands.
Your face is part of sign language. Raise or squeeze your eyebrows for questions.
When the camera is on, the game sees only your hands. Hold each sign still to earn up to three stars.
Let's teach the camera about your hand. Only your hands are shown — everything else is hidden.
Show your open hand, palm facing the camera, fingers spread.
